explanation: An important prophet and leader in Hebrew history, known for receiving the Ten Commandments from God and leading the Israelites out of Egypt.
The Egyptian king who refused to let the Israelites go free, which led God to send ten plagues upon Egypt.
A people descended from the patriarch Israel (Jacob), who were slaves in Egypt and later led out by Moses.
A practice where people are treated as property and forced to work under compulsion without freedom.
Materials used to construct structures and monuments, such as bricks.
A building block made from clay and fired in a kiln, often used as construction material in ancient Egypt.
Dried stalks of grain that were used as a binding agent in brick production.
The amount of work or tasks imposed on an individual or group of people.
A series of disasters and afflictions that God sent upon Egypt to force Pharaoh to release the Israelites.
